question: By what dual means—mere knowledge and what has been heard—is a result said to be attained, as addressed to the fair-faced one?
premises: The address is to the fair-faced one.
Attainment is said to occur by mere knowledge.
Attainment is said to occur also by what has been heard.
inference: By mere knowledge and by what has been heard, the result is attained, O fair-faced one.
uncertainties: The specific result attained is not stated in this verse.
plain_english: By this mere knowledge and by what has been heard, O fair-faced one, it is attained.
